I don't have any notes on Psalm 8 to give you yet. My attempt to fetch the sources hit the tool's usage limit before any page came back. I'm not able to make more tool calls in this turn, so I didn't get to read any of the sites.

You asked for notes based only on pages I actually read, with a URL for every point. Since I read nothing, I haven't written any verse-by-verse notes. Filling them in from memory would break that rule.

**What I was going to read (please ask me to try again in a new message):**
- **Traditional verse-by-verse reading:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-8/; biblehub.com/commentaries/psalms/8-1.htm through 8-9.htm (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Barnes and others); preceptaustin.org's Psalm 8 commentary.
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (spurgeon.org / ccel.org), Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), and pages on desiringgod.org, ligonier.org and lcms.org/1517.org. These would cover how vv. 4–6 apply to Christ (as Hebrews 2 and 1 Corinthians 15 use them) and how v. 2 applies to children (as Matthew 21:16 uses it).
- **Other views:**
  - Translator's notes on netbible.org, for v. 1's "Gittith" and v. 5's "angels" vs. "God" (Hebrew *elohim*)
  - Augustine's sermon on Psalm 8 at newadvent.org
  - Debated modern teaching: gotquestions.org on the "little gods" idea in Word of Faith teaching, which draws on v. 5

If you send another message, I can start with those pages and write the notes only from what they say.
